decisions.rationale: "sporadic breast cancer" is used adjectivally to modify the noun "progression" ("sporadic breast cancer progression"), so it is a disease mention serving as a modifier rather than a standalone disease head.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: "familial breast and ovarian cancer" is a contiguous string referring to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer), so it is annotated as one Composite Mention even though it also modifies "gene".
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2 (Contiguous text strings / Composite Mention)

decisions.rationale: "non-hereditary (sporadic) breast cancer" is the head noun phrase of "cases of" and names one specific disease form (breast cancer of non-hereditary type), with the qualifiers included as the minimum necessary span.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease) and 5 (Minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: "carcinoma in situ" refers to one specific, well-defined disease entity (a stage/type of carcinoma) with no further categorization, so it is a Specific Disease.
"invasive cancer" refers to a family of multiple specific cancers that share the invasive property rather than one definable disease, so it is a Disease Class; "cancer" is retained per the rules.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Disease Class) and What NOT to Annotate 4 (cancer retained)

decisions.rationale: "breast cancer" is used as the disease named in the sentence ("compromised in breast cancer") and is linked to one specific disease definition without further categorization, so it is a Specific Disease.
